explanation: Cheek kissing is a common greeting in Turkey, especially between men in the same social circle (typically twice) and between closer acquaintances generally; between men and women it depends on familiarity and setting, with a handshake preferred in formal or conservative contexts. Hand-kissing — bringing an elder's hand to your forehead — is also a well-regarded way to greet older relatives.
local_tip: Let the other person initiate; mirror a cheek kiss if offered, and default to a handshake with new or more formal acquaintances.
regional_note: Opposite-gender cheek kissing is more accepted in secular, urban circles and less common in conservative or rural settings.

also_check.note: Cheek kissing isn't customary; bowing is the standard greeting.
Cheek kissing (la bise) is common, though the number of kisses varies by region.
Cheek kissing between men is common, but between unrelated men and women it's generally avoided.
